title: What The Purview Data Governance Retirement Means For Your Data Quality
summary: Purview data governance retirement ends support on November 12, 2027. Learn how to keep data quality covered as you move to Microsoft Fabric.
body_markdown:
Historically, Microsoft Purview has been a market leader in enterprise data governance. It gave large organizations one catalog for their data estate, with data quality built in. That model ran governance in a separate catalog that harvested metadata from the platforms it governed. However, the market need has shifted. Over the last few years, every major data platform has folded governance in as a native capability, so data is governed where it is stored. Microsoft’s retirement of Purview data governance brings that shift to its own stack, and the strategy behind it is sound. It also leaves one practical question open. Where do the data quality programs that ran in Purview go next?


As a Microsoft partner, we wrote this post to help teams plan for the Purview data governance retirement.


## What Did Microsoft Announce?


Microsoft just[announced](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-security-blog/a-next-step-in-the-evolution-of-the-microsoft-data-governance-strategy/4572227) that it is retiring Purview data governance. Support ends November 12, 2027, and after that customers lose access.


### What Is Retiring In Purview Data Governance


- Unified Catalog, including data quality, data products, and the glossary
- Data Map
- Workflows
- Classic Azure Purview


### What Is Staying


Purview as a product continues. Only its data governance capabilities are retiring. The security and compliance capabilities stay and keep working with Microsoft Fabric. If you use Purview for sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, data security posture management, or insider risk management, those are not part of this retirement.


### Where Data Governance Goes Next


Microsoft is taking a[lake-first approach](https://www.telm.ai/blog/fabcon-2026-recap-how-microsoft-is-turning-fabric-into-the-control-plane-for-trustworthy-ai-ready-data/) and moving data governance into[OneLake catalog](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/governance/onelake-catalog-overview) in Microsoft Fabric. Microsoft will build all new governance capabilities there, so data is discovered, governed, and secured where it is stored. Databricks, Snowflake, and Google have made the same move with Unity Catalog, Horizon, and Dataplex.


## What Does It Mean For Customers Running Purview?


For teams running Purview today, the data governance retirement touches two things, your catalog and your data quality.


For the catalog, Microsoft has laid out the route. OneLake catalog governs data in OneLake. In a federated estate, data on other platforms can be mirrored or shortcut into OneLake, and data that stays outside is governed through an integrated partner catalog such as Alation, Atlan, Collibra, or Informatica.


Your data quality program takes more planning. Three questions decide how you approach it.


### Do My Rules And Scores Carry Over?


Not automatically. In Purview, data quality rules, scan schedules, and scores are attached to data assets inside Unified Catalog. When Unified Catalog retires, they retire with it.


Microsoft’s announcement does not cover your data quality rules, so you will need to rebuild the ones you keep. Rebuilding fixed-threshold rules by hand repeats the old problem, since they are costly to maintain across thousands of tables and miss anomalies inside a valid range. Drawn from each table’s schema and historical trends, AI-recommended rules adjust their thresholds as the data changes, with no one re-writing them.


### Are My Sources Covered?


Only the ones that are in OneLake.[Mirroring and shortcuts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/onelake/unify-data) can bring other platforms in, but support differs for each source. For enterprises, most critical tables often sit across Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or on-premises databases. Where a connection exists, it usually brings across the curated gold layer. Data issues tend to originate further upstream, in the bronze and silver layers that stay on the source platform. For as long as the estate spans more than OneLake, data quality monitoring has to reach the data where it lives, not only where it lands.


### How Do I Cut Over Without A Coverage Gap?


Purview data quality is supported until November 12, 2027, but production pipelines, reports, and agentic workflows depend on this data, which rules out a hard cutover.


Teams would need to run a program in parallel for the replacement to baseline each table and reach coverage parity with the rules you are keeping. Work back from the date, and treat any rule added in Purview from here as technical debt.


That is the data quality gap in the Purview data governance retirement. It spans what you rebuild, where you monitor and when you start, and it has to close before the catalog migration completes.


## How Telmai Bridges The Data Quality Gap


*See Telmai run as a native workload in Microsoft Fabric.*


Telmai closes this gap as[a native workload for Microsoft Fabric](https://www.telm.ai/integrations/msfabric/) . Instead of rebuilding retired rules one by one, you start with AI-recommended rules on day zero, generated from each table’s schema, catalog metadata and historical trends. Telmai reads OneLake catalog to prioritize the tables that matter most to your team, and learned baselines keep coverage growing with the estate without configuration. Both human users and AI agents get data health insights in real time.


*One Telmai quality layer covers data in OneLake and the platforms around it.*


The native workload monitors data in OneLake, and direct connections cover data outside it. Both feed the same signals to data teams and AI agents. Where your data lives decides which path you take.


### If Your Data Is In OneLake


*Telmai reads through OneLake catalog, so mirrored sources, shortcut sources and OneLake tables are monitored over one connection.*


1. **Add the workload.**[Install Telmai](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/telmaiinc1760440996162.telmai-fabric-data-observability) from the[Workload Hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/workload-development-kit/more-workloads-add) in Microsoft Fabric in a single click. It inherits Entra ID and Fabric workspace roles, with no setup scripts to run. Scans run in place as Spark jobs on your own Fabric capacity, and only operational metadata leaves your tenant.
2. **Let the catalog set priorities.** Telmai reads[OneLake catalog](https://www.telm.ai/integrations/onelake/) to score tables on signals such as downstream Power BI usage, the number of teams that depend on them and lineage. Monitoring starts where business risk is highest.
3. **Monitor from learned baselines.** Monitors track volume, schema, freshness and completeness on Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg tables, and[flag anomalies](https://www.telm.ai/products/data-quality/) from the first scan. Alerts route to stakeholders through Microsoft Teams, Jira and ServiceNow. AI agents query the same signals through Telmai’s MCP server before they act.


### If you are a Fabric customer with hybrid data real estate


*Sources not yet in OneLake, such as Oracle, BigQuery and Redshift, connect directly. Sources exposed through OneLake catalog are read through the catalog. Both feed one quality layer.*


1. **Connect where the data lives.** Telmai[connects directly](https://docs.telm.ai/telmai/connect-to-data) to platforms such as[Snowflake](https://www.telm.ai/integrations/snowflake-data-quality/) ,[BigQuery](https://www.telm.ai/integrations/bigquery-data-quality/) , Redshift and ADLS, with no data copy and no mirroring compute. Monitoring can be live in a few hours.
2. **Monitor upstream.** Cover the bronze and silver layers where issues originate, so they are caught before they reach the gold tables that feed OneLake.
3. **Move to the catalog as tables land.** Any source exposed through OneLake catalog connects through the catalog, and monitors built on direct connections carry over. The same monitors check each table before and after it moves, which is the parity check a migration needs. The result is[one quality layer](https://www.telm.ai/telmai-enterprise-data-quality-platform/) across the estate.


### What To Do With Your Existing Rules


- **Keep the rules that encode business logic.** Start from the SQL-based checks Telmai recommends for each asset, then add the conditions from your Purview rules, so nothing is written from scratch.
- **Retire the generic checks.** Null, freshness and row count rules are covered by Telmai’s built-in completeness, freshness and volume monitors.
- **Run in parallel.** Turn Telmai on alongside Purview now, reach coverage parity, then retire Purview data quality well before November 12, 2027.


For large hybrid data estates, Telmai works with Microsoft partners such as[iLink Digital](https://www.ilink-digital.com/insights/whitepapers/data-trust-on-microsoft-fabric-building-a-trusted-data-foundation-for-the-agentic-era) to map your existing Purview rules to Telmai and move them over without a coverage gap.


## What We Are Seeing In The Field


The paths we’ve laid out are not theoretical. They reflect what we are hearing from enterprise data teams in the field. Here are two recent conversations.


1. A[large insurer](https://www.telm.ai/industry/insurance/) is standardizing hundreds of application teams on Microsoft Fabric. Data quality ships as a starter notebook that each team copies and edits, so checks drift apart and every new rule rolls out one team at a time. Their leadership wants one standard layer for teams to self-serve data quality.
2. A Fortune 500 company runs Snowflake as its core warehouse and copies selected schemas into OneLake. Its checks are hand-built inside individual pipelines, so nothing monitors both platforms or proves a table is intact after it moves. It needs one quality layer across both, with[data kept inside its network](https://docs.telm.ai/telmai/deployment-models/virtual-private-cloud-vpc-deployment) .
